subject: Post-call: scaling constraints, latency SLOs & KV cache behavior
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@sentinel.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + summary from our call — latency & throughput constraints

Hi Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard and next steps so we’re aligned before Ben & Dylan dive into topology sizing.

High-level pain points you shared:
- User-facing search/assist has become unpredictable under peak loads (spikes during batch processing windows).
- Cost of inference on current infra is rising; caching policies are ad-hoc.
- You need deterministic tail latency for customer SLAs (esp. conversational flows).

Goals we captured:
1) P95 latency target: <= 200 ms for short-form completions (<= 256 tokens)
2) Sustained throughput: 400–600 req/s per region during peak with burst to 1k for short windows
3) Support for Llama-70B for hallucination-sensitive flows and a 13B fallback for cost-sensitive paths
4) KV cache reuse across sessions for the same user to reduce repeated computation

Key constraints / red flags you mentioned:
- On-premise data residency for certain PII workloads (may need Private deployment or VPC peering)
- Procurement window: budget commit by end of Q3 (Sept)
- Preference for quantized model variants if quality after int8 is acceptable

Attached: a short SLO proposal PDF and a rough topology sketch (these are preliminary). Ben will follow with a technical deep-dive that covers batching strategy, cache eviction, and concrete latency numbers per model/instance class.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Ben to send a technical topology + sizing note by EOD tomorrow (we called out KV reuse patterns and cache TTL options).
- Dylan to set up a cross-functional call (infra + security) if you want to explore Private options and KMS key flow.
- You to share any existing perf traces or a representative traffic pattern CSV so we can run a quick cost/latency estimate.

Are we aligned on the above? If so, I’ll lock Ben’s deep-dive to tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi | Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sentinel.ai>

Cc: Ops Team <ops@sentinel.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + summary from our call — latency & throughput constraints

Irene — thanks for the tidy summary, that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks: 

- The 200 ms p95 is for the short-form completion path only (confirming). Longer multi-turn flows can tolerate 400–600 ms but we'd still prefer lower where possible.
- For throughput, the 400–600 req/s is per region (US West primarily), but global bursts could route to EU if needed.
- On the KV cache: we absolutely need sticky user-level caches for 24 hours, and eviction only after inactivity; TTL of 24h is a must for our personalization use case.

Questions for Ben / Redwood team: 
1) Do you have examples of production deployments where Llama-70B sustained p95 < 250 ms? If so, what instance types and batching parameters were used?
2) If we go with int8 quantization for 70B, what quality delta should we expect vs fp16 for our extractive QA prompts?
3) For Private deployment, what does KMS integration look like (we use AWS KMS and have strict key policies).

I’ll gather a short traffic sample and upload it to the Drive link you shared. Also including Ops in case they want to schedule the Private-ops call.

—Tom
Tom Reynolds | Head of ML Engineering, Sentinel AI
Sentinel AI • tom.reynolds@sentinel.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sentinel.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + summary from our call — technical deep-dive (topology + SLOs)

Tom — quick technical write-up based on what we discussed and the constraints you confirmed. I’ve kept the math conservative; we can tighten after we see your traffic trace.

1) Example sustained p95 for Llama-70B: we've observed p95 around 220–280 ms for 1–2 token streaming step completions on Nvidia A100x4-style serving (multi-card partitions) with aggressive KV reuse and small dynamic batches (8–16). Key factors: sequence length, kv-cache hit rate, and batching window.

2) Batching & latency tradeoffs:
- Continuous batching with 8–12 ms scheduling window gives good tail isolation. For your target p95 <200ms on 256-token paths, we recommend setting dynamic batch max=16 and max waiting window=10ms; this keeps per-token scheduling overhead low while preserving headroom for bursts.

3) KV cache strategy:
- Sticky per-user cache keys stored in memory-backed shard pools. TTL: configurable; 24h is fine but note memory footprint increases linearly with active users.
- Cache eviction: LRU with explicit TTL + occasional compaction. We can offload cold segments to an SSD-backed local cache if memory budget is constrained (adds ~2–6ms on miss).

4) Quantization guidance:
- int8 for 13B: negligible quality impact for most prompt types (recommended).
- 70B int8: quality may drop on extractive QA edge cases; we recommend running an eval set (we can run your prompts) to measure ROUGE/F1 deltas. If needed, use mixed BF16+int8 for critical layers (slightly higher cost). Attachment "quantization-comparison.xlsx" contains example deltas from similar customers.

5) Private deployment + KMS:
- We support AWS KMS via dedicated VPC peering. Keys remain customer-managed; Redwood agents request signed tokens for model keys. We’ll share a short runbook for key policy allowances.

6) Topology suggestion (high level):
- Ingress LB (region) -> Router that enforces model-routing policies -> Pool A (L70B, 4x card partitions, dedicated KV shards) + Pool B (L13B quantized, denser packing for cost) -> Cache layer (memory-backed per-shard) -> Autoscaler reacts to queue length and p95 breach.
- Draft topology sketch attached (topology-sketch.png) and I added per-pool rough qps capacity.

Next tangible items from our side:
- We’ll run an initial latency/cost estimate after you upload the sample trace (Irene, please flag when available).
- If you want, we can run a small A/B eval: L70B fp16 vs 70B-int8 on a representative prompt set and return quality/lambda metrics.

Forwarding the SLO PDF as promised. If helpful, I can convert these suggestions into a one-page runbook for your infra team.

Cheers,
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
